title: Singleton only for services with no per-operation state
statement: A service is registered `AddSingleton` only when it holds no mutable state that varies per call (or protects that state itself, e.g. behind a lock or by only touching the filesystem per invocation). A collaborator whose behavior is parameterized per use — built around a specific request, agent, or run — is `AddTransient` or `AddScoped` instead.
rationale: A singleton is constructed once and shared by every concurrent request; any field it sets from one call's input becomes visible, and possibly overwritten, by every other concurrent call. `GuidelineStore` is safely a singleton because every method takes `repositoryRoot` as a parameter and touches no shared mutable field; `GuidelineImpactAnalyzer` is `AddTransient` in the same file precisely because it is built to analyze one impact request.

good.code:
builder.Services.AddSingleton<GuidelineStore>();   // stateless: every method takes repositoryRoot as a parameter
builder.Services.AddTransient<GuidelineImpactAnalyzer>();  // built fresh per impact analysis
good.caption: Lifetime chosen by whether the service carries per-call state.

bad.caption: Per-call state on a singleton: concurrent requests overwrite each other's draft.

changelog.summary: Initial rule, grounded in the GuidelineStore/GuidelineImpactAnalyzer lifetime contrast in Program.cs.
